proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:exact\mbox{-}model}\), this law satisfies the propensity-shape condition \(\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}propensity\mbox{-}shape}\) and the multiplier envelope \(\mathrm{ass:multiplier\mbox{-}envelope}\).  The definition of \(r_\kappa\) gives \(r_0(x)=1\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Hence, equation by equation,
\[
 e_P(x)=\frac{r_0(x)g_P(x)}4=\frac{g_P(x)}4,
\]
and
\[
 1\le g_P(x)\le2
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \frac14\le e_P(x)\le\frac12.
\]
Thus strict bounded overlap holds uniformly on the same exact model class; no support or law has been changed.

We next compare the two decision problems.  For any Borel data-only estimator \(T\), define the oracle estimator
\[
 T^e(o_{1:n},e)=T(o_{1:n}).
\]
This map is Borel and simply ignores its second argument.  For every \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), it has exactly the same loss as \(T\):
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left|T^e(O_{1:n},e_P)-\tau_P(0)\right|
 =
 \mathbb E_P\left|T(O_{1:n})-\tau_P(0)\right|.
\]
Taking first the supremum over the common model class and then the infimum over the respective estimator classes in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}risk}\) and \(\mathrm{def:unknown\mbox{-}risk}\) yields
\[
 R_n^e(d,0,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L). \tag{1}
\]
The lower inequality of \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}minimax}\), specialized to \(\kappa=0\), states that for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
 c_e n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le R_n^e(d,0,\beta,\gamma,L), \tag{2}
\]
where \(c_e>0\) is independent of \(n\).  Combining (1) and (2) proves
\[
 c_e n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L). \tag{3}
\]

Now set \(S=\alpha+\beta\) and \(t=\min\{\gamma,S\}\).  The upper inequality of \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\), again specialized to \(\kappa=0\), is attained by the total clipped three-block data-only estimator constructed there and gives, for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le C_1 n^{-t/(2t+d)}, \tag{4}
\]
where \(C_1<\infty\) depends only on the fixed primitive indices and \(L\), not on \(n\).  Equations (3) and (4), with \(c=c_e\) and \(C=C_1\), prove the displayed bracket on the exact class.

Finally, if \(S\ge\gamma\), then \(t=\gamma\), so (3)--(4) become
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le C n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}.
\]
Both sides are constant multiples of the same pure power of \(n\); therefore the matching conclusion contains no logarithmic multiplier.  If \(S<\gamma\), then \(t=S\), and the same argument proves only
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le C n^{-S/(2S+d)}.
\]
No equality of these exponents, and hence no sharp nuisance-dominated rate, follows from the two cited established theorems.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose \(\kappa=0\), and set \(S=\alpha+\beta\) and \(t=\min\{\gamma,S\}\).  Then, for every \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\),
\[
 e_P(x)=g_P(x)/4\in[1/4,1/2]
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
\]
There exist constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and not on \(n\), such that, for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le C n^{-t/(2t+d)}.
\]
Consequently, if \(S\ge\gamma\), then
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
\]
with no logarithmic multiplier.  If \(S<\gamma\), this theorem asserts only the displayed two-sided bracket and does not assert that its upper exponent is minimax sharp.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The asserted all-regime Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman rate is not proved on the exact singleton uniform-design class.  For \(S=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), disjoint partition-local bumps at amplitude \(\delta=\ell^S\) have contrast H\"older scale \(\delta\ell^{-\gamma}=\ell^{S-\gamma}\), which diverges as \(\ell\downarrow0\); overlapping smooth frames do not satisfy the partition-local hypothesis of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1; and filling the transition holes of the published support-modified construction contributes an uncancelled term of order \(nh^d\delta^2\), which diverges at the proposed nuisance rate below the elbow.  Under exactly the same model assumptions, the established oracle converse and first-order data-only estimator prove the stated bracket in every regime and a matching pure-power rate when \(S\ge\gamma\).  This narrows only the conclusion, not the model class.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(\kappa=0\), and set \(S=\alpha+\beta\) and \(t=\min\{\gamma,S\}\).  Then, for every \(P\in\mathcal P(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\),
\[
 e_P(x)=g_P(x)/4\in[1/4,1/2]
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
\]
There exist constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and not on \(n\), such that, for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \le C n^{-t/(2t+d)}.
\]
Consequently, if \(S\ge\gamma\), then
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
\]
with no logarithmic multiplier.  If \(S<\gamma\), this theorem asserts only the displayed two-sided bracket and does not assert that its upper exponent is minimax sharp.
proposed.justification: This is the strongest exact-uniform bounded-overlap consequence of the established oracle converse and total data-only first-order estimator: an all-regime bracket and the exact oracle rate on the smooth-nuisance slice \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).
proposed.gap: When \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), the exact singleton uniform-design class still lacks both a higher-order upper bound and a matching nuisance-dominated lower experiment; the published perforated-support witness does not supply the latter.
proposed.consumer: Researchers using fixed uniform designs obtain a rigorous bounded-overlap bracket in every regime and the sharp pure-power pointwise rate when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\); in rougher nuisance regimes, the theorem deliberately reports the remaining precision gap rather than attributing an unproved rate to a causal forest or R-learner.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the unresolved mixture dependency by the two established theorems that prove the corrected claim, and remove the obsolete published-rate symbol from the theorem's free-symbol set.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The established data-only estimating functional is \(\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\).  With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), it satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}\mathbb E_P\lvert\widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)-\tau_P(0)\rvert\le Cn^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)},\] while the corresponding minimax risk satisfies \[c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}.\] The two powers coincide when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\); the sharper rough-nuisance functional remains the subject of \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The previous metadata asserted the still-open equivalence \(R_n\asymp\rho_n\).  The corrected theorem changes a rate guarantee, so the estimand-functional line must name only the proved estimator and bracket.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give a pointwise H\"older-CATE nuisance-smoothness frontier under bounded overlap over a density-qualified design class; the displayed lower construction in Definition 1 uses a covariate density supported on a perforated set.
Theorem 3 bounds a local-polynomial R-learner under bounded estimated propensities and nondegenerate local Gram matrices.
Theorem 2.1 controls the affinity between two convex mixtures when perturbations localize to a measurable partition.
The random-design variance-functional results use local polynomial U-statistics and a fuzzy lower construction to expose a regression-functional elbow.
Theorem 1 analyzes empirical-Gram higher-order influence-function corrections that remove a covariate-density smoothness requirement for average doubly robust functionals.
Theorem 2 gives near-minimax integrated \(L_1\) rates for random treated and control designs under bounded density ratios and contrast smoothness at most one.
Theorem 1 gives the scalar pointwise regression rate under a regularly varying design density through a local-mass balance.
The weak-overlap results derive thresholded average-effect limit laws and a scalar regression smoothness degradation under propensity-tail restrictions.
Corollary 4 gives pointwise RKHS CATE rates without consistent propensity estimation while retaining a uniform positive overlap parameter.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact-uniform result no longer promises to match the full Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman nuisance frontier; it is an informed-by comparison with an exact smooth-nuisance slice and an unresolved rough-nuisance gap.

prose_updates.tldr: For the exact local-zero model, the proved oracle converse and total first-order estimator give \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), where \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  At bounded overlap \((\kappa=0)\), this becomes a rigorous exact-uniform bracket and closes to \(R_n\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), without a logarithm, when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  The sharper rough-nuisance rate, its critical logarithms, and its same-class full-support product-mixture converse remain open.

project_justification.gap: The closest published pointwise CATE frontier assumes bounded overlap over a density-qualified design class, and its displayed least-favorable density removes nuisance-bump transition regions.  That witness does not prove a nuisance-dominated lower bound on the singleton uniform design, while the overlapping-frame replacement presently lacks a valid fixed-\(n\) product-mixture comparison.
project_justification.niche: Exactly uniform covariates and a known polynomial overlap geometry isolate a local treatment-scarcity experiment.  The current contribution separates what is already certified---the oracle benchmark, an explicit first-order data-only rate, and the full smooth-nuisance slice---from the unresolved higher-order rough-nuisance frontier.
project_justification.fill: The paper provides a total finite-operation estimator and the honest all-regime bracket \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\).  It proves oracle attainment whenever \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\), including the exact-uniform bounded-overlap rate with no logarithm, and records the specific mixture and smoothness obstructions that prevent a sharper claim when \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\).

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Theorems 1--2 and Definition 1, is the closest bounded-overlap pointwise contrast frontier.  Its density-qualified class and displayed perforated-support lower witness motivate the conjectured nuisance elbow but do not establish that lower bound for the singleton uniform design used here.  The present Theorem 3 therefore proves only the bracket supplied by the exact-uniform oracle converse and first-order upper bound, becoming sharp when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  Kennedy2023DRCATE supplies bounded-overlap local-polynomial R-learner motivation, while LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF and ShenGaoWittenHan2020 motivate higher-order projection corrections.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, requires partition-local perturbations and does not directly cover the overlapping smooth frames needed to preserve full support.  GaoHan2020 concerns integrated random-design contrast risk; Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign concerns scalar pointwise regression under a design zero; Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics concerns weak-overlap average-effect inference and scalar regression; and Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE retains a global overlap lower bound.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the application: the official \(\texttt{grf}\) workflow learns nuisance regressions and uses treatment-balance restrictions, but no claim is made that its causal forest attains the rates proved here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The rough-nuisance lower-bound routes fail for structural reasons not repaired by the current core.  Write \(S=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\).  Disjoint partition-local contrast bumps of width \(\ell\) and nuisance-scale amplitude \(\delta=\ell^S\) have H\"older scale \(\delta\ell^{-\gamma}=\ell^{S-\gamma}\), which diverges as \(\ell\downarrow0\).  Overlapping smooth squared frames repair the transition regularity but violate the partition-local premise of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, and their shared signs generate nonzero multi-observation cross terms.  Filling the perforated transition holes instead leaves a product-experiment contribution of order \(nh^d\delta^2\), which diverges at the proposed nuisance rate below the elbow.  Noninteger corner powers and max-norm tie surfaces create additional compensation regularity issues for \(\kappa>0\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established result is the parameterized bracket \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\le R_n\le C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), attained on the upper side by a total clipped three-block estimator.  It is sharp and equals the oracle rate whenever \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\).  In particular, for \(\kappa=0\) this smooth-nuisance slice has rate \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) without a logarithm.  For \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), the higher-order upper rate, matching exact-uniform lower bound, oracle-penalty classification, and critical logarithms remain open; no Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman rate is claimed for that slice.
